newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arab Bank drives Jordanian share index up.
newsitem.headline: Arab Bank drives Jordanian share index up.

text.p: Arab Bank shares rose strongly to fresh 12-month highs on Saturday, almost singlehandedly pushing the official Amman stock exchange index close to its highest level for over three years.

The bank, which accounts for almost a third of total bourse capitalisation, rose five dinars to 275 dinars and drove the index up in an otherwise weak market, accounting for nearly half the day's 1.2 million dinar turnover.

Brokers attribute Arab Bank's strong gains on Wednesday and Saturday to forecasts of strong 1997 profits, expectations of a bonus Arab Bank share offering, and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.79 percent to 163.68 points even though falling stocks outnumbered gainers.
The index is now less than a point off a three-year high of 164.35 recorded at the start of June after a sustained wave of foreign buying.
But this time brokers say the underlying sentiment is less bullish.
"It's a weak market. We expect it will start picking up but not in near future," said Nasser al-Amad, head of United Financial Investment.

He said last week's 0.25 percentage point cut in Jordan's discount rate to 8.25 percent would have to be followed by further decreases before it had a significant effect on the bourse and Jordan's wider investment economy.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 16 to 11 on Saturday, with another 17 traded but closing unchanged.
